name: FS90R continuous-rotation micro servo
description: FEETECH FS90R 9 g micro servo modified for continuous 360° rotation: the pulse width sets speed and direction instead of angle. 50 Hz pulses of 700–2300 µs; 1500 µs = stop (90 µs dead band), shorter pulses turn clockwise, longer pulses counter-clockwise, faster the further from 1500 µs. Runs on 4.8–6.0 V: about 100–130 RPM no load, 1.3–1.5 kgf·cm stall torque, 110–130 mA running and 700–800 mA stalled. Has a trim pot to set the stop point. Sold as: FEETECH FS90R micro continuous rotation servo (Adafruit #2442 / Pololu #2820) with 3-wire lead and JR-style female 2.54 mm plug (brown GND, red V+, orange signal), horns and screws included.
eli5: A small motor that keeps spinning instead of stopping at an angle; your code picks which way it turns and how fast, perfect for robot wheels.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Brown wire: ground (join it to the microcontroller's GND)

pins.name: V+
pins.description: Red wire: servo supply 4.8–6.0 V; up to 800 mA when stalled

pins.name: SIG
pins.description: Orange wire: 50 Hz control pulses, 700–2300 µs (1500 µs = stop); 3.3 V logic works

supplierQuery: FEETECH FS90R continuous rotation micro servo
buildNotes: Wire colours: brown = GND, red = V+ (4.8–6.0 V), orange = signal. The 3.3 V signal from an ESP32 or Pico drives it fine.
Power V+ from a 5–6 V supply (not the 3.3 V pin) that can give 800 mA per servo when stalled; join that supply's ground to the board's GND.
1500 µs should stop it. If it still creeps, turn the trim pot in the recess on the case with a small screwdriver while sending 1500 µs.
Pulses below 1500 µs turn it clockwise, above 1500 µs counter-clockwise (looking at the horn). Speed tops out well before 700/2300 µs.
Don't stall it or back-drive it by hand for long; that can damage the gears and motor.

driver.code:
# FEETECH FS90R micro continuous-rotation servo, MicroPython driver.
# Datasheet (FEETECH FS90R spec): pulse width range 700-2300 us, stop at 1500 us,
# dead band 90 us, CW for 1500->700 us, CCW for 1500->2300 us (seen from the horn side).
# Standard 50 Hz (20 ms) servo frame. Supply 4.8-6.0 V; 3.3 V signal logic works.
# The pulse sets SPEED and DIRECTION, not an angle. If it creeps at stop(), turn the
# trim potentiometer in the case (or pass a different stop_us).
from machine import Pin, PWM

PERIOD_US = 20000  # 50 Hz frame


class FS90R:
    def __init__(self, pin, stop_us=1500, min_us=700, max_us=2300):
        self.stop_us = stop_us
        self.min_us = min_us
        self.max_us = max_us
        self.pwm = PWM(pin if isinstance(pin, Pin) else Pin(pin), freq=50)
        self.pwm.duty_u16(0)  # no pulses: motor off

    def write_us(self, us):
        us = max(self.min_us, min(self.max_us, us))
        self.pwm.duty_u16(int(us * 65535 // PERIOD_US))

    def speed(self, pct):
        """pct -100..100. Negative = clockwise (pulse < 1500 us), positive =
        counter-clockwise (pulse > 1500 us), 0 = stop. |pct| 100 = 700/2300 us."""
        pct = max(-100, min(100, pct))
        if pct < 0:
            us = self.stop_us + (self.stop_us - self.min_us) * pct / 100
        else:
            us = self.stop_us + (self.max_us - self.stop_us) * pct / 100
        self.write_us(int(us))

    def cw(self, pct=100):
        self.speed(-abs(pct))

    def ccw(self, pct=100):
        self.speed(abs(pct))

    def stop(self):
        """Send the 1500 us stop pulse (inside the 90 us dead band)."""
        self.write_us(self.stop_us)

    def off(self):
        """Stop sending pulses: the motor is unpowered and stops."""
        self.pwm.duty_u16(0)

    def deinit(self):
        self.pwm.deinit()

example.code:
import time
from fs90r import FS90R

servo = FS90R({SIG})
servo.stop()
time.sleep(1)
servo.cw(50)    # 1100 us: clockwise, half speed
time.sleep(2)
servo.ccw(50)   # 1900 us: counter-clockwise, half speed
time.sleep(2)
servo.stop()
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
